--------------------------------------------------- --- Feast of Christ the King Today, to mark the Feast of Christ the King, adoration of the Blessed Sacrament will take place in this church from 4.00 pm until 6.00 pm The Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe, also called the Feast of Christ the King, is celebrated on the last Sunday of each Liturgical year. Pope Pius XI, instituted this feast in 1925 to respond to growing secularism and atheism. He recognised that attempting to ‘thrust Jesus Christ and His Holy Law’ out of public life would result in continuing discord among people and nations. This Solemnity encourages us to celebrate and live out our faith in public and reminds us, that while governments come and go, Christ reigns as King forever. Youth 2000 Christmas Retreat 11th – 13th December 2026 Calling all young people aged 16 –35! Join us at the Youth 2000 Christmas Retreat in Newbridge College, Co. Kildare. This is a donation-only event, with free buses available across the country and all meals included. Expect inspiring talks and workshops, Mass, music, prayer, and plenty of opportunities to chill out and meet other young Catholics. Whether you are new to the faith or looking to be refreshed, all are welcome. To register or find out more visit

or follow @Youth2000Ireland. Ireland's 3rd National First Saturdays Conference. This year's conference will take place in Knock on Saturday 28th November. Carraig na bh Fear Community Council Christmas Craft Market Get into the festive spirit at the Carraig na bh Fear Christmas Craft Market, taking place at Scoil an Athar Tadhg on Sunday, 6th December from 12.00 md until 4.00 pm. Browse stalls from local vendors, discover unique Christmas gifts and crafts, enjoy festive treats and hot drinks, and bring the children along for a special visit from Santa. Admission is free and everyone is welcome. History and Heritage Cork’s ‘ Kilmainham’ Gaol Join us on Thursday 26th November at 8.00 pm in Carraig na bh Fear Community Hall for a talk by Eolan Ryng giving a fascinating insight into Cork’s past and the people who helped shape it. Originally built in the 1840s as the Cork Military District Prison, Cork Gaol is the site of the only executions carried out outside Dublin in connection with the 1916 Rising. It tells the stories of Cork’s great heroes – the executions, the hunger strikers, those connected with the ambushes at Clonmult, Dripsey and Mournabbey, and many more inspirational people who played their part in the fight for freedom. Admission free. All are welcome! The 2027 Calendar – A Little Piece of Carraig na bh Fear to Treasure. Our Calendar features the winning photos chosen by you from our competition earlier this year. Each photo is accompanied by a fascinating story and every page features a seanfhocal, taken from the Torna Collection. This calendar costing €10.00 is for sale in local shops. It would make a very special Christmas gift for anyone with a connection to Carraig na bh Fear and is sure to be treasured long after 2027 is past. Carraig na bh Fear

We acclaim Jesus as our King, the one who died for us and rose triumphant. We offer praise and worship and ask for the grace to live as worthy citizens of his kingdom of justice, truth, love and peace. ( Credit to " The Under The Ambo Book".) By proclaiming Christ as King at the end of the yea r, the church prepares its heart for Advent, shifting from the ce lebration of Christ's present reign to anticipating his second c oming.
